note: Window agent p2000-p2009, 2 Nov 2026: five events, two keyframe overrides and one ruling; every entry rests on a page opened in this run. Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: events/2 redated to December 2005 and taken from the Iraqi Republic; events/0 note corrected (10 of the 61 cells lie on the land border).

region.text: Mexico's land: the cells whose centres lie south of the Rio Grande

events.note: The page says 'the continental border then follows the middle of the Rio Grande', so the south bank is Mexico's. The start anchor of 2000 gives 61 cells whose centres lie in Mexico (Chihuahua 17, Coahuila 15, Tamaulipas 14, and others: 51 along the river from Ciudad Juarez to the Gulf and 10 along the land border west of El Paso) to the United States, and the 2006 keyframe of the United States then drops them to nobody, a hole in Mexico from 2006. This returns them to Mexico from 1 January 2000; the cause is the border fit of the 1980s United States shape (the anchors of 1980 to 1999 already hold the 61 cells), a no-op if an earlier window has fixed it.

region.text: the United States side of the Rio Grande within 5 km (New Mexico, Texas, Colorado): US land that mexico/ledger/9 took with a 5 km river strip

events.note: 24 November 2009: 'the U.S. ceded 6 islands in the Rio Grande to Mexico'; the page gives no area and 'the continental border then follows the middle of the Rio Grande'. mexico/ledger/9 resolves the six islands as the whole Rio Grande plus 5 km, which gave Mexico 96 United States cells (New Mexico 44, Texas 34, Colorado 14) although the river runs wholly inside the United States above El Paso. Six river islands are far smaller than one 253 km2 cell, so no cell changes hands: this returns the strip to the United States in the same month (a dossier request asks for the region of ledger/9 to be fixed).

region.text: the three governorates of Erbil, Sulaymaniyah and Duhok that the Region holds as a federal region

events.note: 15 October 2005: the constitution recognised the Kurdistan Region as a federal region 'while preserving its existing authorities established in 1992', among them the Kurdistan Regional Government, and the page gives no transfer of land. iraqi-republic ledger/14 (a 'gain' of the Region, October 2005) hands the Region's 146 cells to the Iraqi Republic, whose dissolve at the end of 2005 passes 144 of them to the Republic of Iraq and leaves 2 nobody's, so the Region owns no land from 2005 although its own 1992-2013 keyframe and the hierarchy row (constituent of Iraq, 2005-2026) say it keeps it. Dated December 2005 so that it comes after ledger/14 and before the dissolve at year end, and taken from the Iraqi Republic, which still holds the cells then: the Region keeps all 146 cells, drawn as a constituent of Iraq from the end of 2005 (the reviewer moved it from 1 January 2006 and the Republic of Iraq, which left the end of 2005 wrong and 2 border cells nobody's). The window p2010-p2019 has the same event dated 1 January 2010, a no-op after this one.

region.text: Ituri, the north-east of Orientale round Bunia (a 180 km disc about 50,000 km2 of the district's 65,000)

events.note: The page: 'Ugandan troops remained in the DRC in early 2003, despite the Luanda Agreement of the previous year' and the UPDF 'stormed the regional capital Bunia on 6 March 2003'. The dossier closes the whole Ugandan zone (Orientale and Equateur, 3,338 cells) at the Luanda Agreement of 6 September 2002 because it found no withdrawal date; this reopens Ituri, where the page puts the withdrawal at 2 June 2003 (next event). Applied after the dossier's own September event.

region.text: Ituri, the north-east of Orientale round Bunia (a 180 km disc about 50,000 km2 of the district's 65,000)

events.note: 2 June 2003: 'Uganda withdrew from Ituri on 2 June 2003' (the page); the war ended on 18 July 2003 with the Transitional Government. Closes the Ituri occupation reopened in September 2002.

union.text: the Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, including the part east of the 180th meridian

correction.text: Russia with Chechnya (the dossier's own correction, unchanged) plus Chukotka east of 180 degrees, which the Cliopatria outline leaves out

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's Russian Federation shapes stop at the 180th meridian, so the 412 cells of Chukotka east of it (the page: Chukotka is 'the easternmost federal subject of Russia' and 'the only part of Russia lying partially in the Western Hemisphere'; 'In 1991, Chukotka declared its separation to become a subject of the Russian Federation in its own right') are dropped at the keyframe snap and become nobody's. Same cut as the p1990-p1999 overrides of the 1991, 1992, 1995 and 1996 keyframes.

union.text: the Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, including the part east of the 180th meridian

correction.text: the 2006 Cliopatria shape (with Chechnya), holding 2006-2013, plus Chukotka east of 180 degrees, which the outline leaves out

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's Russian Federation shapes stop at the 180th meridian, so the 412 cells of Chukotka east of it (the page: Chukotka is 'the easternmost federal subject of Russia' and 'the only part of Russia lying partially in the Western Hemisphere'; 'In 1991, Chukotka declared its separation to become a subject of the Russian Federation in its own right') are dropped at the keyframe snap and become nobody's. Same cut as the p1990-p1999 overrides of the 1991, 1992, 1995 and 1996 keyframes. The shape holds 2006-2013, so the override reaches into p2010-p2019 (the 2014 and 2024 shapes need the same union).

region.text: Maakhir, the eastern Sanaag coast incorporated into Puntland in January 2009

rulings.why: The page: 'In January 2009, the short-lived quasi-state of Maakhir was officially incorporated into Puntland.' Puntland's 2009 keyframe claims Maakhir but Somaliland's whole-protectorate keyframe claims the same 66 cells and the smaller state won; Somaliland had no administration there (the page says only that control of the western Sool, Sanaag and Ayn provinces is disputed with Somaliland).
